newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to mull new rules for oil, gas industries.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to mull new rules for oil, gas industries.

text.p: Brazil's government will probably send Congress in November a new version of a bill regulating the opening of the country's gas and oil industries, said lower house deputy Eliseu Resende.

"We are holding public hearings to see what investors and politicians want to change. The government is likely to send the new version by November," said Resende, a Liberal Front Party (PFL) deputy who is drawing up a new bill for the lower house's Petroleum Committee.

An older version of the bill was seen offering privileges to state monopoly Petrobras. For example, under the old draft, Petrobras would automatically win any tender to develop oil and gas fields if its proposals were competitive with bids from private companies.
Resende said his bill would seek to change the Petrobras bias and include changes to rules for importing petroleum derivatives.
It would also give more power to the National Petroleum Agency, which would act as a regulatory body for the entire sector.
Resende said public hearings would end in October.
